name: The Book of the Wars of the Lord

verses.t: The Book of the Wars of the Lord is named in the Law, and the book itself is lost.

Numbers 21:14–15 says: “Therefore it is said in the book of the wars of the Lord, What he did in the Red sea, and in the brooks of Arnon, And at the stream of the brooks that goes down to the dwelling of Ar, and lies upon the border of Moab.”
The citation stands in the wilderness itinerary, after Israel turned north toward the land of Moab, and before the song of the well at Beer.
What follows in Numbers is the song itself, and the victories over Sihon king of the Amorites and Og king of Bashan — wars the lost book appears to have commemorated.

Numbers 21:14–15 says: “Therefore it is said in the book of the wars of the Lord, What he did in the Red sea, and in the brooks of Arnon, And at the stream of the brooks that goes down to the dwelling of Ar, and lies upon the border of Moab.” The citation stands in the wilderness itinerary, after Israel turned north toward the land of Moab, and before the song of the well at Beer.

verses.t: No manuscript of the Book of the Wars of the Lord has been found. Ancient writers knew the title from Moses; they did not possess the work.

It is counted among the lost books of Israel, with the Book of Jashar (which later collections tried to supply) and the chronicles of the kings that the canonical histories mention and do not reproduce.

Some have thought it a collection of battle-songs, like the song of the well, or the taunt-song over Heshbon that Numbers records next. Others have thought it a prose chronicle of the Lord’s wars from the sea to the Jordan.
What can still be read is the canonical witness: that Israel kept a book by this name, that it spoke of the Red Sea and of Arnon, and that Moses could point to it as already known.
Here the path of this reader pauses, then continues with Deuteronomy. The wars are not forgotten; they are kept in the Law that remains.

verses.t: From the King James Bible, the surrounding passage (Numbers 21:10–35) is given here so the lost book is not read without its only surviving quotation.
And the children of Israel set forward, and pitched in Oboth. And they journeyed from Oboth, and pitched at Ijeabarim, in the wilderness which is before Moab, toward the sunrising.

From from there they removed, and pitched in the valley of Zared. From from there they removed, and pitched on the other side of Arnon, which is in the wilderness that comes out of the coasts of the Amorites: for Arnon is the border of Moab, between Moab and the Amorites.

Therefore it is said in the book of the wars of the Lord, What he did in the Red sea, and in the brooks of Arnon, And at the stream of the brooks that goes down to the dwelling of Ar, and lies upon the border of Moab.
And from from there they went to Beer: that is the well whereof the Lord spoke to Moses, Gather the people together, and I will give them water.
Then Israel sang this song, Spring up, O well; sing you to it: The princes dug the well, the nobles of the people dug it, by the direction of the lawgiver, with their staves.

And from the wilderness they went to Mattanah: And from Mattanah to Nahaliel: and from Nahaliel to Bamoth: And from Bamoth in the valley, that is in the country of Moab, to the top of Pisgah, which looks toward Jeshimon.
And Israel smote Sihon with the edge of the sword, and possessed his land from Arnon to Jabbok, even to the children of Ammon: for the border of the children of Ammon was strong.

And they possessed his land, and dwelt in all the cities of the Amorites, in Heshbon, and in all the villages of it. And Moses sent to spy out Jaazer, and they took the villages of it, and drove out the Amorites that were there.
And they turned and went up by the way of Bashan: and Og the king of Bashan went out against them, he, and all his people, to the battle at Edrei.

And the Lord said to Moses, Fear him not: for I have delivered him into your hand, and all his people, and his land; and you shall do to him as you did to Sihon king of the Amorites, which dwelt at Heshbon.
So they smote him, and his sons, and all his people, until there was none left him alive: and they possessed his land.
